question:
A 43-year-old female presents to the emergency department with acute onset right-sided weakness
that developed over the past two hours. She reports diminished strength in her right hand compared to
her left, along with progressive weakness in her right leg. Her medical history includes diabetes,
hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension, for which she admits poor medication compliance. Physical
examination reveals decreased muscle strength on the right side compared to the left, with preserved
reflexes bilaterally. The patient demonstrates right-sided lower facial droop and inability to smile,
though forehead wrinkling remains intact. Given these clinical findings and history, which additional
symptom would you expect to find in this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Dysarthria (B) Conjugate gaze
deviation to the left (C) Lateral strabismus (D) Nystagmus with fast component to the right (E) Medial
strabismus (F) Homonymous hemianopia (G) Paralysis of upward gaze (H) Flaccid paralysis of the
tongue (I) Internuclear ophthalmoplegia (J) Vertical diplopia
 A. Vertical diplopia
B. Nystagmus with fast component to the right
C. Conjugate gaze deviation to the left
D. Internuclear ophthalmoplegia
E. Flaccid paralysis of the tongue
F. Dysarthria
G. Medial strabismus
H. Homonymous hemianopia
I. Paralysis of upward gaze
J. Lateral strabismus
